configurePresets.name: linux-asan-o1
configurePresets.description: The nightly's AddressSanitizer leg (docs/testing.md, Nightly checks): address only, so its runtime options and its slowdown are its own, at -O1 with frame pointers kept and without -DNDEBUG, so every assert runs. cmake/icl/IclSanitizers.cmake adds -O1 -fno-omit-frame-pointer to every sanitizer build; the flags are repeated here so the optimisation level is written where it is read.

configurePresets.name: linux-ubsan
configurePresets.description: The nightly's UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer leg: undefined alone, -fno-sanitize-recover=all (from IclSanitizers.cmake, so the first report fails the run), -O1 and no -DNDEBUG.

configurePresets.name: linux-static-analysis
configurePresets.displayName: Linux, Debug, for clang-tidy and cppcheck
configurePresets.description: Debug (assertions on, so their code is analysed), no Tracy, the game on. Its compile_commands.json is what run-clang-tidy and cppcheck read (tools/ci/static_analysis.py). Nothing here is run.

configurePresets.name: linux-gcc-analyzer
configurePresets.description: The library libs/core built with GCC's static analyzer (-fanalyzer): no Qt (the analyzer is slow and noisy on Qt headers) and no tests. Build only. CXX must be g++, GCC 14 or newer; GCC 14 reports false positives for C++ standard library code that later releases do not, so the baseline is the CI's compiler's.

configurePresets.name: linux-release-perf
configurePresets.description: linux-release with the performance tests (label perf) built. A separate build directory, so the ordinary test run never sees them. Run: ctest --preset linux-release-perf; summary: python3 tools/ci/perf_report.py (docs/testing.md).

configurePresets.name: windows-msvc-release-perf
configurePresets.description: windows-msvc-release with the performance tests (label perf) built. A separate build directory, so the ordinary test run never sees them. Run: pwsh tools/dev/test.ps1 -Perf (docs/testing.md).

configurePresets.name: windows-msvc-profile
configurePresets.displayName: Windows, MSVC, optimised with symbols, Tracy on
configurePresets.description: The game as it ships, plus Tracy: what to build to take a profile (docs/profiling.md). Starts profiling at launch, listens on the loopback interface only, and builds tracy-capture and tracy-csvexport for the host. Never a release.

configurePresets.name: linux-profile
configurePresets.displayName: Linux, optimised with symbols, Tracy on
configurePresets.description: As windows-msvc-profile, without the command-line tools (add profiling-tools to VCPKG_MANIFEST_FEATURES for them). CI builds and tests this to keep the instrumentation compiling.

configurePresets.name: windows-msvc-analyze
configurePresets.displayName: Windows, MSVC, /analyze with the C++ Core Check rules
configurePresets.description: Build only. PREfast (/analyze) with the EspX engine, which brings the C++ Core Guidelines checker and its default rules; /analyze:WX- keeps the warnings from failing the build (the baseline decides, tools/ci/static_analysis.py). CMAKE_CXX_FLAGS replaces CMake's own default flags, so those are repeated first. /wd4702 (unreachable code) is off because the analysis pass reports it for test code that the ordinary build does not, and the project builds with /WX. C26446, C26472, C26481, C26482 and C26821 are off: each asks for the Guidelines Support Library (gsl::at, gsl::narrow_cast, gsl::span), which the project does not use, and they were 670 of the first 987 findings. The warnings are read from the build log by tools/ci/static_analysis.py. Headers in angle brackets (Qt, vcpkg, the standard library) are external and not analysed.

configurePresets.name: macos-asan-ubsan
configurePresets.displayName: macOS, Apple Clang, AddressSanitizer and UBSan, -O1

configurePresets.name: ios-release
configurePresets.description: An iPhone or iPad (arm64), built by Xcode on a Mac. Unsigned: it needs no Apple account (a signed build is the release workflow's). vcpkg's toolchain is the toolchain file, as everywhere (VCPKG_ROOT is a vcpkg checkout at the baseline of vcpkg.json; CI's setup-vcpkg action sets it). No tests and no command-line program are built: nothing runs on a device here.

configurePresets.name: ios-game-release
configurePresets.displayName: iOS game (device, Release, unsigned, Qt static)
configurePresets.description: The whole game on an iPhone or iPad (arm64), built by Xcode on a Mac against Qt's static iOS kit. Unsigned unless given the signing variables (the release workflow passes HEART_BOOM_MATHS_IOS_SIGNING_TEAM, _PROFILE, _BUILD_NUMBER and _GAME_CENTER on the command line, docs/ios.md): it needs no Apple account. Needs HEART_BOOM_MATHS_QT_IOS_ROOT (the ios kit of the pinned Qt version) and ICL_QT_ROOT (the macOS desktop kit of the same version, which Qt uses as its host tools). No tests are built: vcpkg is not used and nothing runs on a device here. apps/ios, the one-screen stub, is not built.

configurePresets.name: wasm-core
configurePresets.displayName: WebAssembly, the rules and the text harness, to run under Node
configurePresets.description: libs/core and the text harness built with Emscripten alone (no Qt, no vcpkg), so the golden replays can be checked under Node: `node build/wasm-core/libs/core/heart_boom_maths_harness.js --check libs/core/tests/data/replays`. Needs EMSDK (an activated emsdk).

configurePresets.name: wasm-release
configurePresets.description: The game in a browser, built with Qt's single-threaded WebAssembly kit. Needs EMSDK (an activated emsdk of the Emscripten release the kit was built with: 5.0.5 for Qt 6.12.0, which the kit insists on), HEART_BOOM_MATHS_QT_WASM_ROOT (the wasm_singlethread kit) and ICL_QT_ROOT (the desktop kit of the same Qt version, which Qt uses as its host tools). The finished site is build/wasm-release/site. No tests are built: vcpkg is not used and a browser cannot run them.

configurePresets.name: android-base
configurePresets.description: An Android phone or tablet, built from any host with Qt's Android kit (HEART_BOOM_MATHS_QT_ANDROID_ROOT, for example Qt/6.12.0/android_arm64_v8a: the kit names the architecture), a desktop kit of the same Qt version for the host tools and androiddeployqt (ICL_QT_ROOT), the Android SDK (ANDROID_SDK_ROOT), the NDK that kit was built with (ANDROID_NDK_ROOT) and a JDK 17 or later. `cmake --build --preset <name>` makes the packages. No tests are built: vcpkg is not used and nothing runs on a device here. The C++ module dependency scan is off: nothing here uses modules.

configurePresets.name: android-arm64-release
configurePresets.description: What a release is made from: an unsigned APK and AAB. A package signed with the upload key needs QT_ANDROID_SIGN_AAB (or QT_ANDROID_SIGN_APK) and the QT_ANDROID_KEYSTORE_* environment variables, which only the tag build has (docs/releasing.md).

configurePresets.name: android-arm64-debug
configurePresets.description: A debuggable APK signed with Android's own debug key, which installs on any device that allows apps from outside the store.
